title: Pre-bicam budget meet with economic managers sought
summary: Lawmakers should have a “pre-bicameral” meeting with the country’s economic managers before they overhaul the proposed budget program for 2027, including by ridding it of P54…
byline: Neil Jayson Servallos, Marc Jayson Cayabyab

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — Lawmakers should have a “pre-bicameral” meeting with the country’s economic managers before they overhaul the proposed budget program for 2027, including by ridding it of P54 billion in allocations for multi-purpose buildings (MPBs) and P85 billion for fragmented cash aid, Sen. Panfilo Lacson said.

In an interview with dzBB radio, Lacson questioned the need to fund 3,950 more MPBs next year, stressing that the government has already spent P770.9 billion on 79,816 MPBs since 2012. This amounts to about 48 MPBs for every city and municipality and 973 for every province.
“Where do we dump all these MPBs? We don’t have real estate, especially in Metro Manila and urban cities. It doesn’t make sense anymore,” Lacson said.

With economic growth slowing to 2.1 percent and inflation hitting 7.8 percent, Lacson said the 2027 budget – crafted under earlier macroeconomic assumptions – no longer matches with current realities and must be realigned toward growth-oriented projects before the bicameral conference committee convenes.

“We should sit down first – economic managers, appropriations committee of the House and the finance committee of the Senate – to have discussions before the bicam because that’s where the real battle is fought,” he said.

He disclosed that his team has so far flagged at least 30 MPBs with double or multiple appropriations, including in Zambales and Pangasinan, as well as a shoreline protection project in Zamboanga that carried a P100-million allocation in the House version without grid coordinates and a separate P95-million item in the Senate version sharing the same coordinates.

In addition to scrapping duplicate projects and the P85 billion in non-4Ps fragmented ayuda – such as MAIFIP, TUPAD and AICS – Lacson reiterated his push for the restoration of the Growth Equity Fund (GEF) for fourth- and fifth-class municipalities, which the Senate trimmed to P8.7 billion from P10.3 billion in the National Expenditure Program and House version. “The situation is difficult. These are extraordinary times,” he said.
At Malacañang, Palace press officer Claire Castro urged Lacson to provide information about what he claimed were possible ghost projects in the proposed 2027 national budget.

“Since these are suspected ghost projects, it would be better for Sen. Lacson to inform the DPWH (Department of Public Works and Highways) about the suspected ghost projects or the possible anomalies he saw,” Castro said at a media briefing.
“The President will not allow any anomalous project that would lead to the wastage of public funds and place money on the pockets of the greedy,” she added.
Castro explained that a repeated appropriation is not the same as double appropriation as some projects are implemented in multiple phases.

“We need to authenticate what Sen. Lacson saw because it would be a big help to the government if it is removed. The President would not hesitate to veto it and remove it from the budget if it is really anomalous,” she said. — Alexis Romero, Bella Cariaso
